mainTopic: Mourning practices: overturning beds, the דרגש, the mourner's house, and funeral rules for the honor of the poor
overview: This amud first finishes a ruling about an אבל who must keep doing business. It then turns to כפיית המטה, overturning the beds during mourning. רבי אליעזר says the beds are overturned when the body leaves the house, while רבי יהושע says it happens when the grave is closed. Further ברייתות teach that the beds are stood up before שבת, are overturned again on מוצאי שבת, and that every bed a mourner owns is overturned, apart from special cases like a storage bed and a דרגש. The גמרא works hard to define a דרגש. It finally explains it as a leather bed with loosenable straps and rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A mourner who sleeps on the floor instead has not fulfilled the obligation. Next comes a ברייתא about cleaning and spices in a בית האבל. A new משנה then gives funeral rules for חול המועד. The גמרא explains these with a series of תקנות that made rich and poor do the same thing מפני כבודן של עניים, and the last of these continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: A mourner's business: cut back if he can
steps.stepSummary: Finishes the earlier ruling: if the אבל can reduce his business he should, and if not he may continue it together with the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is able to cut down on his business, he should cut down. If not, he may carry on with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling from the previous discussion about an אבל who needs to keep doing business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The best option is for the אבל to reduce his business. If that is not possible, he is allowed to keep going, but together with the others, not on his own. This closes that topic before a new ברייתא begins.

keyTerms.meaning: he may carry on, keep things moving

phrases.english: If he is able to reduce his business
he should reduce it,
and if not
he may carry on together with them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the others he is doing business with, from the earlier part of this discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a topic carried over from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל should reduce his business if he can; if not, he may continue it together with others.

steps.title: When do mourners begin overturning their beds?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says once the body leaves the house; רבי יהושע says once the grave is sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: From when do the mourners overturn their beds? From when the body leaves the doorway of the house, says רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: from when the grave is closed with its cover.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא records a מחלוקת about the moment the mourners must start כפיית המטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the beds get overturned; they only argue about the starting point. For רבי אליעזר it begins as soon as the body leaves the house. For רבי יהושע it begins later, once the burial is finished and the גולל closes the grave.

keyTerms.meaning: overturning the beds, a mourning practice
the cover stone that closes the grave

steps.confusionAlert: "He leaves the house" means the dead person's body being carried out, not a mourner leaving.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From when do they overturn the beds?
From when he goes out of the doorway of his house,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person who died, being carried out for burial.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
From when the grave cover is sealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵאֵימָתַי כּוֹפִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the business ruling ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: overturning starts when the body leaves the house. רבי יהושע: it starts when the grave is sealed.

steps.title: The story of רבן גמליאל הזקן's funeral
steps.stepSummary: When רבן גמליאל הזקן died, רבי אליעזר told them to overturn the beds when the body left the house. When רבי יהושע told them later, they said they had already done it following רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident when רבן גמליאל הזקן died. Once his body left the doorway of his house, רבי אליעזר told them: Overturn your beds. Once the grave was closed, רבי יהושע told them: Overturn your beds. They answered him: We already overturned them by the word of the Elder.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a real story that shows the two opinions from the last step being applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each רב gave the instruction at the moment his own opinion says it begins. Because רבי אליעזר's moment came first, the people had already done it by the time רבי יהושע spoke. In this story, the practice followed רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident, a story that happened
by the word of the Elder

steps.whatToRemember: There are two possible starting points for כפיית המטה: when the body leaves the house (רבי אליעזר) or when the grave is closed (רבי יהושע). In the story, the people followed רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: There was an incident when Rabban Gamliel the Elder died,
once he was taken out of the doorway of his house,
Rabbi Eliezer said to them:
Overturn your beds.
And once the grave cover was sealed,
Rabbi Yehoshua said to them:
Overturn your beds.
They said to him:
We already overturned them by the word of the Elder.
phrases.notes: "The Elder" here means רבי אליעזר, who had told them earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the מחלוקת from step 2 being applied in a real event.
steps.raayaObject: The two opinions on when כפיית המטה begins
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבן גמליאל הזקן's funeral, where the beds were overturned at רבי אליעזר's word

steps.title: Standing the beds back up on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: on ערב שבת the mourners stand their beds upright from מנחה time onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: From when do they stand the beds back up on ערב שבת? From מנחה time and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא asks when, before שבת, the overturned beds are set back to normal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mourning practices like the overturned bed are not kept on שבת, so the bed has to be turned back before שבת starts. The ברייתא allows this from מנחה time on ערב שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאֵימָתַי זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: From when do they stand the beds upright on Erev Shabbos?
From Minchah time onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵאֵימָתַי זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After learning when overturning begins, we learn when it pauses for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב שבת the beds are stood upright from מנחה time onward.

steps.title: Wait until dark to sit on the bed
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא: even though the bed is stood up from מנחה, the mourner does not sit on it until it gets dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר הונא said: Even so, he does not sit on it until it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר הונא adds a limit to the ברייתא from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning the bed upright early is allowed, but actually sitting on it as a normal bed waits until nightfall, when שבת has begun. So setting the bed up and using it happen at two different times.
steps.confusionAlert: He is not arguing with the ברייתא. The bed may still be stood up from מנחה; he only adds that the mourner waits until dark to sit on it.

phrases.english: Rabbah bar Huna said:
Even so,
he does not sit on it
until it gets dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר הוּנָא: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bed may be stood up from מנחה, but the mourner does not sit on it until dark.

steps.title: Overturning the bed again after שבת
steps.stepSummary: On מוצאי שבת the mourner overturns the bed again, even if he has only one more day of mourning left.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on מוצאי שבת, even though he has only one day left to sit, he goes back and overturns the bed again.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching continues past שבת and says what the mourner does once שבת ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the bed was only stood up because of שבת, mourning picks up again afterward. Even if just one day is left, the mourner still turns the bed back over. Being close to the end does not cancel the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: he goes back and overturns it again

steps.whatToRemember: Before שבת the bed is stood up from מנחה, but the mourner sits on it only after dark. After שבת it is overturned again, even if only one day of mourning is left.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the שבת break pauses the mourning practices without ending them, even when very little of the mourning time remains.

phrases.english: And at the end of Shabbos,
even though he has
only one day left to sit,
he goes back and overturns it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לֵישֵׁב אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from before שבת (steps 4-5) to after שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On מוצאי שבת the mourner overturns the bed again, even with only one day of mourning left.

steps.title: A mourner overturns all of his beds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a mourner must overturn every bed in his house, even ten beds in ten places. If one of five brothers dies, all the brothers overturn their beds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a mourner who overturns his bed does not overturn only his own bed. He overturns every bed in his house. Even if he has ten beds in ten places, he overturns all of them. Even if there are five brothers and one dies, all of them overturn their beds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us how wide the rule of overturning beds goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps covered when the beds are overturned. This ברייתא covers which beds: not just the one he sleeps on, but every bed he owns, wherever it is. It also says every mourner overturns his own beds, so five brothers means five households of overturned beds.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturns his bed, a sign of mourning

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: one who overturns his bed,
does not overturn only his own bed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל מִטּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ הוּא כּוֹפֶה.
phrases.english: rather he overturns all the beds he has in his house.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ עֶשֶׂר מִטּוֹת בַּעֲשָׂרָה מְקוֹמוֹת —
phrases.english: And even if he has ten beds in ten places,
he overturns all of them.
And even if there are five brothers and one died,
all of them overturn their beds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when beds are overturned to which beds must be overturned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner overturns every bed he owns, in every location, and each mourning brother does the same.

steps.title: Exceptions: a storage bed and a דרגש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a bed used only for storing things does not need to be overturned. A דרגש is stood up instead of overturned. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says you loosen its loops and it falls down by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a bed is set aside for storing things, he does not need to overturn it. A דרגש does not need to be overturned; instead he stands it up. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: with a דרגש, he loosens its loops and it falls down by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now lists beds that are treated differently from regular beds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A storage bed is not used for sleeping, so it is left alone. A דרגש is still part of the mourning rule, but its practice is different: the תנא קמא says to stand it up, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to loosen its loops so it collapses. The unusual word דרגש sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A special kind of bed, explained in the next steps

steps.confusionAlert: The דרגש is not exempt from mourning. It is simply handled differently: stood up or let down, not flipped over.

phrases.english: And if it was a bed set aside for storing things,
he does not need to overturn it.

phrases.aramaic: דַּרְגֵּשׁ — אֵין צָרִיךְ לִכְפּוֹתוֹ, אֶלָּא זוֹקְפוֹ.
phrases.english: A דרגש: he does not need to overturn it; rather, he stands it upright.
רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
With a דרגש, he loosens its loops,
and it falls down by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with exceptions to the general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A storage bed is not overturned. A דרגש is stood up (or, per רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, its loops are loosened so it falls).

steps.title: What is a דרגש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word דרגש means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a דרגש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the strange word דרגש from the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot understand why a דרגש is treated differently until we know what it is. So the גמרא stops to define the term.

phrases.english: What is a דרגש?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term used in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word דרגש.

steps.title: עולא: a good-luck bed
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that a דרגש is a 'bed of good luck'.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is a good-luck bed.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question and defines a דרגש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, a דרגש is a decorative bed kept in the house for good luck, not a bed people use. That would explain why it is not overturned like a normal bed.

phrases.english: עולא said: a bed of good luck.
phrases.notes: A bed set up in the house for good fortune, not one that people sat or slept on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דרגש is a good-luck bed, not normally used.

steps.title: רבה challenges עולא from the king in mourning
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks: a משנה says that at a king's mourning meal, everyone sits on the ground but the king reclines on a דרגש. If a דרגש is an unused good-luck bed, would we suddenly seat him on it only now that he is mourning?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: if so, what about the king? We learned in a משנה: all the people recline on the ground, and he reclines on the דרגש. Is there something we never sat him on until now, and now we sit him on it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks עולא's definition using a משנה about a king in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a דרגש is a bed nobody uses, it makes no sense that a mourning king, of all times, would be seated on it. The משנה shows a דרגש is something people actually sit on, which contradicts עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (if your explanation is right)

phrases.english: רבה said to him: but if so,
regarding a king, as we learned:
phrases.notes: סנהדרין 20a. The משנה is talking about the mourners' meal served to a king who is in mourning.

phrases.english: all the people recline on the ground,
and he reclines on the דרגש.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּעַד הָאִידָּנָא לָא אוֹתְבִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Is there something that until now we did not seat him on,
and now we seat him on it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as an unused good-luck bed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has a mourning king reclining on a דרגש. It is unreasonable that he would first be seated on an unused bed specifically while mourning, so a דרגש must be something normally used.

steps.title: רב אשי rejects רבה's challenge using the mourner's meal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says רבה's question is no real difficulty. Just as a mourner is fed by others only now that he mourns, he can also be seated on the good-luck bed only now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: What is the problem? It is just like eating and drinking. Until now we did not feed him or give him drink, and now we do feed him and give him drink!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on רבה's question from Step 11 and says it is not actually a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה thought it was strange to seat a mourning king on a bed nobody uses only now, when he is mourning. רב אשי answers that mourning already brings new treatment: others feed the mourner his meal, which never happened before. So a new kind of seating at that time is not strange either, and עולא's explanation survives.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it, a forceful pushback
It is just like… (comparing to a similar case)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objects to this:
What is the difficulty?
phrases.notes: He means: what is so hard about רבה's question from Step 11?

phrases.english: It is just like eating and drinking,

phrases.aramaic: דְּעַד הָאִידָּנָא לָא אוֹכְלִינֵּיהּ וְלָא אַשְׁקִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: that until now we did not feed him or give him drink,
phrases.notes: This is the mourner's first meal after the burial, which other people give him.

phrases.english: now we feed him and give him drink!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's challenge from Step 11 and so defends עולא's definition.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה's challenge only; עולא's definition is not yet proven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה assumed that new treatment beginning at mourning is strange. Feeding the mourner shows that mourning does bring new treatment.

steps.title: Why isn't the good-luck bed overturned like every bed?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a better challenge. If a דרגש is a regular (good-luck) bed, the rule that a mourner overturns all beds in his house should require overturning it, yet the ברייתא says it is only stood up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty. We learned: a דרגש does not need to be overturned, rather he stands it up. If it is a good-luck bed, why does it not need to be overturned? Didn't we learn: one who overturns his bed overturns not only his own bed, but all the beds in his house!
steps.whatsHappening: After throwing out רבה's question, רב אשי raises a stronger challenge against עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 taught that a mourner overturns every bed in his house. Step 8 taught that a דרגש is only stood up. If a דרגש were just a bed kept for good luck, it should be included in 'every bed' and overturned like the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the real difficulty
A bed of good luck (עולא's definition of דרגש)

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty,
as we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from Step 8.

phrases.english: A דרגש does not need to be overturned,
rather he stands it up.
And if it is a bed of good luck,
why does it not need to be overturned?
Didn't we learn:
One who overturns his bed,
does not overturn only his own bed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל מִטּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ כּוֹפֶה!
phrases.english: but rather overturns all the beds he has in his house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבה's rejected challenge with a new challenge against עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as a 'bed of good luck'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A good-luck bed is a bed. All beds in the house must be overturned, so why is the דרגש only stood up?

steps.title: Not a problem: a bed not used for sleeping is not overturned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second challenge. A good-luck bed is like a bed set aside for storing things, which also does not need to be overturned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? It is just like a bed set aside for storing things, as it was taught: if it was a bed set aside for storing things, he does not need to overturn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the challenge from Step 13 by comparing the good-luck bed to a storage bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'overturn all beds' covers beds that are used for sleeping. Step 8 already showed that a bed used only for storing things is left alone. A good-luck bed that nobody sleeps on fits into that same exception, so the ברייתא saying the דרגש is not overturned causes no trouble for עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed set aside only for storing things

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a good-luck bed stops being a bed. It is still a bed, but like a storage bed it falls under the exception for beds no one sleeps on.

phrases.english: And what is difficult?
It is just like a bed set aside for storing things.
As it was taught:
If it was a bed set aside for storing things,
he does not need to overturn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קַשְׁיָא? מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמִּטָּה הַמְיוּחֶדֶת לְכֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the 'overturn all beds' challenge.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge forgot that beds not used for sleeping, like storage beds, are exempt from overturning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a bed set aside for storing things (Step 8)

steps.title: The real difficulty: what loops would a good-luck bed have?
steps.stepSummary: The final, strong challenge: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says you loosen a דרגש's loops and it falls down. A simple good-luck bed has no such loops.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, a דרגש, he loosens its loops and it falls down by itself. And if you think it is a good-luck bed, what loops does it have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the strongest challenge against עולא's explanation. Step 16 responds with a new definition of דרגש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes a דרגש as having loops that hold it up, so it collapses when they are loosened. That suggests a different kind of object, built with loops. A plain good-luck bed has no loops, so his words do not fit עולא's definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Loops or straps that hold something up
If it enters your mind, if you think

steps.whatToRemember: Two challenges to עולא were rejected (the king's meal and 'overturn all beds'). The challenge that stands is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'loops,' which do not fit a simple good-luck bed.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A דרגש: he loosens its loops
and it falls down by itself.
And if you think it is a bed of good luck,
what loops does it have?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי קַשְׁיָא הָא קַשְׁיָא: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 14 rejected the previous challenge, this offers a new and stronger one.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's definition of דרגש as a 'bed of good luck'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a דרגש has loops that can be loosened. A plain good-luck bed has no loops, so the definition does not fit.

steps.title: A leather-market expert says a דרגש is a leather bed
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל, who spent a lot of time in the leather market, explains that a דרגש is a leather bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came down to בבל, one of the Sages, רב תחליפא from the West, who was often found in the leather workers' market, told him: What is a דרגש? It is a leather bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The good-luck-bed explanation was just disproved. Now the גמרא brings a new answer to 'what is a דרגש?': it is a leather bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leather bed has leather straps tied through loops, so it fits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's words that you 'loosen its loops and it falls'. That is exactly the detail that sank the good-luck-bed explanation. The man's work in the leather market shows why he would know this.

keyTerms.meaning: From the West, meaning from ארץ ישראל
The market of the leather workers
When he came (from ארץ ישראל to Bavel)

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the accepted definition of דרגש, and the rest of the sugya builds on it.

phrases.english: When Ravin came
one of the Sages said to him,
and his name was Rav Tachlifa from the West,
phrases.notes: 'The West' is how the scholars in בבל referred to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: who was often found in the leather workers' market:
What is a dargash?
A leather bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the good-luck-bed definition that step 15 disproved with a new definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A leather bed, which has loops that can be loosened.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה explains how a דרגש is built differently from a bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says a דרגש's straps go through the inside of its frame, while a regular bed's straps wrap over the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי ירמיה said: A דרגש has its strapping from inside it; a bed has its strapping over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from another אמורא that a דרגש is a strapped bed whose straps can be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a דרגש the straps pass through holes in the frame, so you can loosen them and the bed sags down. On a regular bed the straps wrap around the wooden frame and cannot be loosened that way, so it must be overturned. This matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's description.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (brings a supporting statement)
From inside it, through holes in the frame
Over it, wrapped around the outside

phrases.english: It was also stated,
Rabbi Yirmeya said:
A dargash has its strapping from inside it,
phrases.notes: The straps run through holes in the frame itself, so they can be loosened.

phrases.english: a bed has its strapping over it.
phrases.notes: Here the straps are wrapped around the wood, so they can't simply be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the leather-bed definition of step 16 by describing its construction.
steps.raayaObject: The definition of דרגש as a bed with loosenable straps.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ירמיה's description of how a דרגש and a bed are strapped.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a דרגש is handled by loosening its loops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what a דרגש is, the גמרא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא (step 8), both opinions agree that a דרגש is not overturned. They only argue about what to do instead: the תנא קמא says to stand it upright, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says to loosen its loops so it falls by itself. The halacha follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so the mourner loosens the loops instead of standing it up.
steps.whatToRemember: A דרגש is a leather bed with straps through its frame. A mourner loosens the straps so it falls; he does not overturn it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
phrases.notes: His view is the one from step 15: loosen the loops of a דרגש and it falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling once the definition of דרגש is settled.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For a דרגש, the mourner loosens its loops so it falls, following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: A bed with tall posts only needs to be stood up
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי rules that a bed whose posts stick out far only has to be stood upright, not overturned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רבי אסי: A bed whose posts stick out, he stands it up and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ruling from the same teacher about a special kind of bed that also does not need to be overturned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some beds have very long posts, so even upside down the bed stays high off the ground. For such a bed, standing it on its side is enough. Like the דרגש, it is still a bed, but the way the mourner handles it is different.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא
phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha said
that Rabbi Asi said:
A bed whose posts stick out,
he stands it upright and that is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second bed that, like a דרגש, does not need to be overturned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bed with long, protruding posts only needs to be stood upright during mourning.

steps.title: Sleeping on a chair, mortar or floor does not count
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a mourner who sleeps on a chair, a large mortar, or the ground has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who sleeps on a chair, on a large mortar, or on the ground has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a mourner who sleeps somewhere uncomfortable instead of on an overturned bed. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think sleeping on the floor is even harder than an overturned bed, so it should count. The ברייתא says no: he has still not done what he was supposed to do.

keyTerms.meaning: He has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: The point is not about comfort. Even though the floor is less comfortable than an overturned bed, it still does not count.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sleeps on a chair,
on a large mortar,
or on the ground,
has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָשֵׁן עַל גַּבֵּי כִּסֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to handle different beds to whether other uncomfortable sleeping places can replace overturning the bed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner who sleeps on a chair, a mortar or the ground has not fulfilled his mourning obligation.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains: he never overturned the bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the ברייתא: the obligation is to overturn the bed, and this mourner did not do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because he did not fulfill the overturning of the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains why the ברייתא says sleeping on the floor does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה is the act of כפיית המטה, overturning the bed, not just being uncomfortable. Someone who sleeps on the floor but leaves his bed standing has skipped the actual מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturning the bed, a mourner's obligation

steps.whatToRemember: A mourner's obligation is to actually overturn the bed (or loosen a דרגש, or stand up a tall-posted bed). Sleeping somewhere uncomfortable does not replace it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Because he did not fulfill the overturning of the bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁלֹּא קִיֵּים כְּפִיַּית הַמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the ruling of the ברייתא in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The obligation is the act of overturning the bed, so sleeping elsewhere does not fulfill it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The mourning obligation is defined by overturning the bed, not by how uncomfortable the mourner is.

steps.title: Cleaning is allowed in a mourner's house, but incense and spices are not brought in
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows sweeping, sprinkling and dish-washing in a בית האבל, but forbids bringing in incense and spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In a mourner's house, people may sweep the floor and sprinkle water on it. They may also wash bowls, cups, jugs and pitchers there. But they may not bring incense or spices into the mourner's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא listing what may and may not be done in the house of an אבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Basic cleaning is allowed, because the house still has to function. Incense and pleasant smells are a form of enjoyment and comfort, so they are kept out of the mourner's house.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkling water on a dirt floor

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may sweep and sprinkle in the house of the mourner,
phrases.notes: Sprinkling means putting water on a dirt floor so the dust stays down.

phrases.english: and one may wash bowls and cups
jugs and pitchers in the house of the mourner.
But one may not bring incense
or spices into the house of the mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of overturning the bed to other practices in the mourner's house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cleaning and dish-washing are allowed in a בית האבל; bringing in incense and spices is not.

steps.title: A ברייתא of בר קפרא seems to allow bringing spices in
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא's ברייתא forbids only the ברכה over spices in a בית האבל, which implies that bringing them in is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But בר קפרא taught: One does not say a ברכה over incense or spices in a mourner's house. That means only the ברכה is forbidden, but we do bring them in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from the last step with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא only talks about not making a ברכה. The גמרא reads that as implying the spices are present, so bringing them in must be allowed. That contradicts the first ברייתא, which forbids bringing them at all.
steps.confusionAlert: בר קפרא never openly says 'you may bring spices.' The challenge is built on an inference: if only the ברכה is forbidden, then bringing them in must be allowed.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't bar Kappara teach:
One does not bless over incense
nor over spices in the house of the mourner.
It is blessing that we don't do,
but bringing them in, we do bring!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 22 that incense and spices may not be brought into a בית האבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בר קפרא forbids only the ברכה, which implies the spices may be present. That contradicts a ban on bringing them in.

steps.title: The two ברייתות speak about different houses
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא is about the mourner's own house; בר קפרא's is about the house of the consolers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. This ברייתא is about the mourner's house, and that ברייתא is about the house of the consolers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the mourner's own house, spices are not brought in at all. In the house where the consolers gather, spices may be brought in, but no ברכה is said over them. So the two ברייתות do not argue.
steps.whatToRemember: Mourner's house: no incense or spices at all. Consolers' house: they may be brought in, but no ברכה is said over them.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is in the house of the mourner,
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא, which forbids bringing spices in.

phrases.english: that is in the house of the consolers.
phrases.notes: This is בר קפרא's ברייתא, where spices may be there but no ברכה is said.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל, הָא בְּבֵית הַמְנַחֲמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source applies to a different location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seem to speak about the same house, so they appear to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on bringing spices applies to the mourner's own house; the ban on only the ברכה applies to the consolers' house.

steps.title: Food is brought to mourners in plain baskets, not fancy dishes
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that food brought to a mourner is carried in ordinary baskets, not on trays, bowls or narrow baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Food is not brought to the mourner's house on a tray, in a bowl, or in a narrow-mouthed basket, but in ordinary baskets.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us how food should be carried to a mourner's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three kinds of containers that may not be used and one plain container, baskets, that should be used. The משנה itself does not give a reason here.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One does not bring [food] to the house of mourning
not on a tray, and not in a bowl,
and not in a narrow basket, but in baskets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens after the discussion of the ברייתות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food for the mourners is brought in plain baskets, not on trays, in bowls, or in narrow-mouthed baskets.

steps.title: No mourners' blessing on חול המועד, but comforting still happens
steps.stepSummary: On חול המועד the ברכת אבלים is not said, but people still stand in a row to comfort the mourners, and the mourners dismiss the crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: On חול המועד, the mourners' blessing is not said. But people do stand in a row and comfort the mourners, and the mourners send the crowd home.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with what is and is not done for mourners during חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formal mourners' ברכה is held back because of the מועד. But the basic act of comforting in a row still takes place, and the mourners release the many people who came.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of a Festival

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד: no ברכת אבלים, but the row of comforters still forms, and the mourners dismiss the crowd.

phrases.english: And one does not say the mourners' blessing on the Festival days,
but they stand in a row and comfort,
and they dismiss the many.
phrases.notes: The mourners tell the crowd of comforters they may go home now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכת אבלים is not said on חול המועד, but people still comfort the mourners in a row, and the mourners dismiss the crowd.

steps.title: The bier is not set down in the street
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on חול המועד the bier is not set down in the street, so a הספד won't start. A woman's bier is never set down, out of respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not put the bier down in the street, so people won't be drawn into a eulogy. And a woman's bier is never put down, because of respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more rule for a funeral on חול המועד: don't stop and set the bier down in the street. It adds that a woman's bier is never set down, on any day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting the bier down in the street would draw a crowd and start a הספד, which is held back on חול המועד. The rule about women is not tied to the festival at all. It applies always, because of the honor of the dead woman.

keyTerms.meaning: The bier, the bed or frame the dead person is carried on
A eulogy, a speech of mourning for the dead
So as not to encourage or get people used to something

steps.confusionAlert: The first rule is only for חול המועד. The rule about women's biers says לעולם, meaning it applies on every day of the year.

phrases.english: We do not set down the bier in the street
so as not to encourage the eulogy
and not those of women, ever
phrases.notes: He means a woman's bier is never set down in the street, not even on a regular weekday.

phrases.english: because of honor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of mourning rules for חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חול המועד the bier is not set down in the street. A woman's bier is never set down, out of respect.

steps.title: Everyone brings food in plain willow baskets
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how the rich once brought food to a mourner in silver and gold baskets while the poor used willow baskets. The חכמים ruled that everyone must use willow baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: At first, people brought food to the mourner's house differently. The rich used silver and gold baskets, and the poor used wicker baskets of peeled willow. The poor were embarrassed. So the חכמים made a rule that everyone brings food in wicker baskets of peeled willow, to protect the honor of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that gives the background to the משנה's rule about using plain baskets for a mourner's food (step 25).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fancy baskets made the difference between rich and poor public, right at a sad moment. The תקנה took that difference away by giving everyone the same simple basket. This explains why the משנה requires ordinary baskets.

keyTerms.meaning: Baskets, here fancy ones of silver and gold
They instituted, meaning the חכמים made a new rule (תקנה)
The honor and dignity of the poor

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for all three ברייתות here: when a custom shames the poor, the חכמים change it for everyone.

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught
At first they would bring to the house of the mourner
phrases.notes: It means the first meal brought to the mourners after the burial.

phrases.aramaic: עֲשִׁירִים — בִּקְלָתוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁל זָהָב
phrases.english: the rich, in baskets of silver and of gold

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲנִיִּים — בְּסַלֵּי נְצָרִים שֶׁל עֲרָבָה קְלוּפָה
phrases.english: and the poor, in wicker baskets of peeled willow
and the poor were embarrassed
They instituted that everyone should bring
in wicker baskets of peeled willow
because of the honor of the poor

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מוֹלִיכִין בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins and explains the earlier משנה rule about using plain baskets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone brings food to the mourner in plain willow baskets, for the honor of the poor.

steps.title: Everyone serves drinks in colored glass
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: the rich once served drinks in a mourner's house in white glass and the poor in colored glass. The חכמים ruled that everyone uses colored glass.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: At first, in the mourner's house, the rich served drinks in clear white glass and the poor in colored glass. The poor were embarrassed. So the חכמים made a rule that everyone serves drinks in colored glass, to protect the honor of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with the same pattern, this time about the cups used for drinks in the mourner's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White, clear glass was the costly kind and colored glass was the cheaper kind. Once again the חכמים moved everyone down to the simpler option so that nobody's poverty would be on display.

keyTerms.meaning: Serve drinks, giving people something to drink
White, clear glass, the more expensive kind

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught
At first they would serve drinks in the house of the mourner
the rich, in white glass
and the poor, in colored glass
and the poor were embarrassed

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ הַכֹּל מַשְׁקִין בִּזְכוּכִית צְבוּעָה
phrases.english: They instituted that everyone should serve drinks in colored glass
because of the honor of the poor

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַשְׁקִין בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא that applies the same idea to drinking cups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone serves drinks in the mourner's house in colored glass, for the honor of the poor.

steps.title: Everyone's face is covered at a funeral
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: rich people's faces were once left uncovered when they died, while poor people's faces were covered because famine had darkened them. The חכמים ruled that everyone's face is covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, people left the faces of the rich uncovered and covered the faces of the poor, because the poor people's faces had turned dark from famine. The poor were embarrassed. So the חכמים made a rule to cover everyone's face, to protect the honor of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: A third example of the same pattern, this time about the dead person's face: the חכמים ruled to cover every face, rich or poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering only the poor marked them out as poor, because hunger had darkened their faces. Covering everyone hides the difference. All three ברייתות show one principle: change the custom for everyone so the poor are not shamed.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncover, leave open to be seen

steps.whatToRemember: Three תקנות, one pattern: food baskets, drinking cups, and covering the face. In each, everyone follows the simpler way, מפני כבודן של עניים, so that the poor are never shamed in a time of mourning.

phrases.english: At first they would uncover the faces of the rich
phrases.notes: He means the faces of people who had died, during the funeral.

phrases.english: and cover the faces of the poor
because their faces were blackened
because of famine
and the poor were embarrassed
They instituted that everyone's face should be covered
because of the honor of the poor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series with a third example of the same principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone's face is covered at a funeral, for the honor of the poor.

steps.title: Rich and poor carried their dead out differently
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins another example of a gap between rich and poor at funerals: the rich would carry their dead out for burial on a fancy דרגש.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, the rich would carry out their dead on a דרגש, and the poor...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is starting its next example of rich and poor doing things differently at funerals. This line only sets up the case; the sentence keeps going to tell what the poor used and what the חכמים decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as Steps 28-30: first describe the old custom, where the rich did something showy that the poor could not afford, and then give the חכמים's fix. Here the new topic is the thing the body is carried out on. The rich used a fancy דרגש, so the poor were shown up at the most painful moment.

keyTerms.meaning: A fancy couch or bed the rich used to carry the dead out for burial
They would carry out the dead for burial

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Wait for the next line to see what the poor used and what the חכמים ruled.

phrases.english: At first, the rich would carry out (the dead)
phrases.notes: Carrying the body out for burial. The ברייתא doesn't say 'the dead' out loud, but that's what it means.

phrases.english: on a dargash, and the poor...
phrases.notes: A דרגש is a fancy couch or bed. The sentence goes on next with what the poor used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Steps 28-30 with a fourth example of a rich-versus-poor funeral custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The old custom was that the rich carried their dead out on a fancy דרגש. The contrast with the poor and the חכמים's ruling come next.
